title: Tamsin and the Promise
premise: Xanthe Galloway built her wedding-planning empire on the ruins of her own broken engagement, orchestrating other people's happily-ever-afters while refusing her own. When a freak snowstorm traps her at a remote Catskills venue with Julian Ashe—the rival planner poaching her clients and the man she loved and abandoned a decade ago—old promises and old wounds thaw together. As they collaborate to save a high-profile wedding from disaster, Xanthe discovers Julian's return is no accident: he's dying of a degenerative illness and came back to settle what they left unfinished. Choosing love over the safety of invisibility, she risks everything—her company, her reputation, her carefully guarded heart—and in the final chapter, marries him in the very venue where it all began, trading borrowed pieces of herself for the whole heart.
about_author: Dominic Quintana is a former hotel event manager who spent fifteen years watching strangers fall in and out of love in ballrooms before turning those observations into fiction. He writes from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where snowstorms are frequent and second chances are a local specialty.

chapters.title: The Vow She Sells
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At a lavish Manhattan wedding she's orchestrated flawlessly, Xanthe watches the bride cry genuine tears of joy and feels nothing but professional pride and private hollowness. A rival firm's card appears in the groom's pocket—Ashe & Co. The beat: competence as armor, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Client List
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian Ashe reviews his stolen client files and finds Galloway Events everywhere, always one step ahead. He requests the Hollowbrook Inn contract specifically—a venue with history only he understands. The beat: ambition tangled with an older, unadmitted motive.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Good Timing
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Flashback woven through present-day prep: the engagement she broke off at twenty-four, the promise made on a porch in the rain, the vow never to need anyone that much again. Her assistant notices she flinches at Julian's name. The beat: memory as both wound and compass.

chapters.title: Hollowbrook Bound
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both planners arrive at the remote Catskills inn for a make-or-break client weekend, each believing the other canceled. Their first face-to-face in ten years is all polished hostility over canapé samples. The beat: rivalry as a language for things neither will say.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The storm hits early and hard; roads close, cell service dies, and the client party cancels. Stranded with staff gone home, Xanthe and Julian are the inn's only occupants besides its eccentric owner, Dot. The beat: forced proximity stripping away escape routes.

chapters.title: Dinner by Candlelight and Combat
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Over improvised dinner, they trade barbs that turn into confessions by dessert—careers built, marriages avoided, the industry that ate their twenties. Xanthe catches Julian hiding tremors in his left hand. The beat: intimacy disguised as argument.

chapters.title: The Porch, Again
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Snowbound, they find the inn's porch mirrors the one from their past. Julian almost tells her why he really took this job; instead he asks about the promise she broke. Xanthe deflects with a story that's half-true. The beat: the past pressing against the present like weather against glass.

chapters.title: What the Storm Digs Up
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Digging out the cellar, they unearth Dot's box of forty years of wedding photographs—including one of Xanthe's parents' wedding, which she never knew was held here. Shaken, she admits her cynicism has roots deeper than her broken engagement. The beat: identity revealed as inheritance, not choice.

chapters.title: A Truce Written in Frosting
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Bored and thawing toward each other, they agree to co-plan a mock wedding for Dot's anniversary as practice for their shared future clients. Working side by side, their old creative chemistry reignites alarmingly. The beat: collaboration as courtship neither names.

chapters.title: The Hand That Slips
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian drops a tray during the mock reception; Xanthe steadies him and sees the tremor up close. He lies badly. Alone, he rereads a neurologist's letter hidden in his luggage—early-onset Huntington's, progression faster than hoped. The beat: dread beneath the warmth, ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They spend a night talking until dawn, exchanging truths in careful increments—she gives him her mother's story, he gives her his father's. Both feel the danger of it. Xanthe recognizes she's doing exactly what she swore not to: lending pieces of her heart instead of risking the whole. The beat: self-awareness without yet the courage to change.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Roads reopen; the real client reschedules. On the last morning, a kiss in the kitchen doorway that neither apologizes for. But Julian pulls back when Xanthe starts making plans—he knows something she doesn't. The beat: joy shadowed by concealment.

chapters.title: Back to the City, Back to War
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In Manhattan, their firms clash publicly over the Meridian Hotel account, and Xanthe wonders if the storm was a hallucination. Julian is distant on calls. Her business partner warns her he's seen this pattern before—her, falling, then fleeing. The beat: reality reasserting itself, doubt creeping in.

chapters.title: The File on Ashe
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Investigating Julian's poaching, Xanthe finds his firm is nearly bankrupt and that he bought the Hollowbrook contract through a shell company tied to—her old venue. He planned this reunion. Fury floods in before questions do. The beat: betrayal misread, tension spiking.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Rain Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Xanthe ambushes Julian at an empty event space. He confesses he engineered the storm weekend but refuses to say why, and she walks out. Alone, he finally reads the letter aloud to the empty room, practicing how to tell her. The beat: climax of misunderstanding; the truth one sentence away and withheld.

chapters.title: Dot's Letter
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Dot mails Xanthe a note Julian asked her to hold 'if I lose my nerve': the truth of his diagnosis and his real reason for returning—to give Xanthe the chance to refuse him honestly, the chance she never gave him at twenty-four. The beat: devastating clarity; every prior scene reframed.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian collapses at a site inspection; a client films it, and gossip spreads through the industry. He assumes Xanthe will now stay away out of pity or fear. He begins dismantling his firm quietly. The beat: rock bottom, isolation chosen to protect her.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe burns her prepared speech about betrayal and instead shows up at his hospital room with the mock-wedding binder and Dot's photos. She tells him she's done lending pieces: she wants all the time there is, however much that is. The beat: the theme crystallized—love as risk, not guarantee.

chapters.title: Merging Houses
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They merge their firms into one small studio and announce it to a skeptical industry. Xanthe fights to keep Julian's name on the door; he fights his own fear of being remembered as a cautionary tale. The beat: rebuilding identity together, power shared rather than wielded.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Almost Wasn't
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Their biggest client threatens to walk unless they prove stability; a rival leaks Julian's diagnosis. In a crisis meeting, Xanthe chooses radical honesty—telling the client everything—and gambles the whole company on it. The client stays, moved. The beat: climax of the external plot; corruption of image-consciousness defeated by truth.

chapters.title: Promises, Kept This Time
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. At Hollowbrook, in the same hall as Dot's anniversary party, Julian proposes properly—finishing the promise from ten years ago, word for word, that Xanthe once interrupted. She says yes before he finishes. The beat: memory redeemed; the circle closed deliberately.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Promise
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Epilogue a year later: their own small wedding at Hollowbrook, Julian steady enough to dance one full song, Dot as witness. Xanthe, planning weddings again, finally believes in them—not as guarantees, but as acts of courage. Final line echoes the blurb: staying invisible was never really an option. The beat: resolution, bittersweet and luminous.
